obtained.how: NOAA Fisheries' own free PDF of the Fishery Bulletin article (spo.nmfs.noaa.gov; the fisherybulletin.nmfs.noaa.gov link now redirects to the journal's home page)

bibliography.checked_against: the title page (p. 80) and the running head
bibliography.note: Fish. Bull. 97:80–91 (1999); issue 1 in the running head ('Fishery Bulletin 97(1), 1999'). Authors K. E. Limburg, M. L. Pace, K. K. Arend.

claims.claim: white perch larvae in the Hudson died at Z = 0.044–0.785/d (median ~0.27) across 6-day hatch cohorts
claims.location: p. 86 (PDF p. 7), Table 2 (read on the page image)
claims.conditions: New Hamburg site (river km 105) only, spring–early summer 1994; Z fitted as exponential decline of each 6-d hatch cohort's density (bongo tows, 500-µm mesh, otolith ages); white perch cohorts A–H: 0.785, 0.509, 0.328, 0.241, 0.304, 0.187, 0.044, 0.137
claims.note: Median of the eight = (0.241 + 0.304)/2 = 0.27. The extremes are weak: cohorts A (0.785) and H (0.137) rest on two samples each with no SE, and G's 0.044 is a non-significant fit (r² 0.21, P 0.70); the authors say earliest and latest cohorts 'were poorly estimated'. The five well-estimated cohorts (B–F) give 0.19–0.51/d. The rates are per day by the article's use of G/Z with G per day; Table 2 itself prints no unit.

claims.claim: the white perch rates fell as water warmed from 12 to 21 °C
claims.location: p. 84 (PDF p. 5), Results (Recruitment potential at New Hamburg); temperatures from p. 86 (PDF p. 7), Table 3
claims.quote: For white perch, mortality rates declined more or less monotonically with time
claims.conditions: calculated cohort water temperatures 12.2 °C (cohort B, 5 May) to 20.8 °C (H, 11 June); the sentence continues 'and therefore also with increasing temperature'
claims.note: 'Tidal fresh water' in the table's Water column: the article says white perch occur in the oligohaline and freshwater sections and does not give New Hamburg's salinity; 'tidal Hudson River at New Hamburg' is safer.

claims.claim: larval growth 0.155–0.331 mm/d by date at New Hamburg
claims.location: p. 83 (PDF p. 4), Table 1 (read on the page image)
claims.conditions: mean somatic growth rate (mm/d) of the larvae caught on each date, from otolith ages; New Hamburg, 24 May–6 July 1994; n = 9–47 fish per date
claims.note: Growth rose from before to after the Bosmina bloom; GR = −0.050 + 0.013 × mean water temperature (r² 0.15, n = 774, both species).

claims.conditions: all three sites pooled (Kingston, New Hamburg, Haverstraw Bay); site means 0.209, 0.215 and 0.245 mm/d (p. 84)
claims.note: The overall mean is for all sites, not New Hamburg alone; the row reads as if both refer to New Hamburg. New Hamburg's own mean is 0.215 mm/d.

notes: Other values: white perch instantaneous growth G 0.125–0.378/d by cohort and G/Z 0.25–8.5 (Table 3); white perch G was correlated with zooplankton density (G = 0.136 + 4.64×10⁻⁴ × zooplankton/L, r² 0.96), the bloom peaking at 520 copepods + Bosmina per litre; mean G/Z 0.35 before, 1.27 during and 2.53 after the bloom (not significantly different). The companion paper, Limburg et al. 1997, is cited for the larvae's diet (see that entry).
